standard: PEC 2017 - Article 2.20 receptacle and motor loads, Article 4.30, Article 4.45
note: Scalar rules the generator set sizing relies on, each from a printed PEC 2017 page.
receptacleVoltAmperesPerOutletSource: 2.20.2.5(I) and (L): receptacle outlets at not less than 180 volt-amperes for each single or each multiple receptacle on one yoke.
bankOfficeReceptacleSource: 2.20.2.5(K): in banks or office buildings the receptacle load is the larger of 2.20.2.5(I) or 11 volt-amperes/m2.
receptacleDemandSource: 2.20.3.5 and Table 2.20.3.5: first 10 kVA or less at 100%, remainder over 10 kVA at 50% (non-dwelling receptacle loads).
motorFeederSource: 4.30.2.4: conductor ampacity of not less than 125% of the highest-rated motor full-load current plus the sum of the other motors' full-load currents plus 100% of the noncontinuous non-motor load plus 125% of the continuous non-motor load.
generatorOutputSource: 4.45.1.13: conductors from the generator terminals to the first distribution device(s) have an ampacity of not less than 115% of the nameplate current rating of the generator; 100% where the design of the generator does not permit overloading.
defaultGeneratorPowerFactorNote: Not from the PEC. 0.8 lagging is the usual rating basis of a standby generator set; use the nameplate value of the set you intend to buy.
motorStartingDefaultsNote: Not from the PEC, confidence verify. 20% is a typical subtransient reactance for a diesel standby set; use the data sheet of the set you intend to buy. 15% is the PEC's own limit for a fire pump motor at starting (6.95.1.17), used here only as a starting point; many designers allow less to keep lighting steady.
lockedRotorBasis: Locked-rotor kVA comes from Table 4.30.14.5(B) (polyphase, Design B, C and D) and Table 4.30.14.5(A) (single-phase), the PEC's maximum locked-rotor currents by horsepower and voltage. The PEC publishes them for selecting disconnecting means and controllers (4.30.9.10, 4.40.1.2, 4.40.5.1, 4.55.1.8(C)), so they are upper values for starting; the nameplate code letter (Table 4.30.1.7(B)) or the maker's data gives the real figure, which the starting current percentage lets you use.
voltageDipBasis: Voltage dip = X"d x S / (Sgen + X"d x S), with S the locked-rotor kVA of the motors that start together and Sgen the kVA of the set. The set needed for a dip of at most D% is X"d x S x (100/D - 1). This is the usual engineering approximation, not a PEC formula, and the running load already on the set is not subtracted from its capacity.
